config.prompt: Explain, in a few paragraphs, how a write-ahead log lets a database recover after a crash.

reference.text:
A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
When a database crashes, the log can be used to recover the database to a consistent state. The database can be restored to a point in time just before the crash by replaying all the changes recorded in the log up to that point. This ensures that the database is consistent and up-to-date, even if the database itself was corrupted or lost.
The write-ahead log also provides a way to recover from partial failures, such as a disk failure that causes some but not all of the database files to be lost. In this case, the log can be used to recover the lost data by replaying the changes recorded in the log. This ensures that the database is consistent and up-to-date, even if some of the database files are lost.
